methods.title: FO01 — Extract the grammar, then remove the example
methods.source_block:
## FO01 — Extract the grammar, then remove the example

**Inputs:** An exemplar, inspected predecessors, intended users and the valued function.

**Operation:** Describe components, relations and constraints. Mark inherited parts. Write the smallest rule that allegedly explains a useful difference. Remove the exemplar and use that rule to construct three meaningfully different instances.

**Construction:** Turn a successful maze level into a rule about controlling what arrival accomplishes, then vary destination, timing and capacity.

**Comparison:** Equal information and budget with examples alone, ordinary decomposition and an existing equivalent principle.

**Outcome:** Valid useful descendants after duplicate/equivalent mechanisms are removed; shared relation and distinct consequences.

**Defeating observation:** Only the original instance works, variants repeat its surface, or the extracted grammar is an established equivalent with no new opening for the intended users.

**Basis:** FS10, FS13. **Claim target:** reusable generation, distinct from worldwide originality.

methods.title: FO02 — Invert one exclusion, retain its purpose
methods.source_block:
## FO02 — Invert one exclusion, retain its purpose

**Inputs:** A convention that excludes a proposed family and the reason for that convention.

**Operation:** Express the exclusion literally. Reverse or relax one condition. Preserve its valued purpose through a different relation. Construct an old-compliant example and two varied examples using the changed rule.

**Construction:** Replace the assumption that every monster's purpose is attacking the hero with a public delivery objective, while preserving threats and meaningful strategic costs.

**Comparison:** Ordinary goal-based enemy design and a version that merely renames attacking. If a competent existing rule already permits the same actions, claim an access/representation change instead of formal expansion.

**Outcome:** Distinct feasible choices and a family whose members remain legible and useful.

**Defeating observation:** Relaxation breaks the valued function, creates arbitrary exceptions or only reveals options already available under the unchanged rule.

**Basis:** FS10; prior destructive-to-creative research. **Claim target:** a specified constraint change.

methods.title: FO03 — Build a bridge to an adjacent audience
methods.source_block:
## FO03 — Build a bridge to an adjacent audience

**Inputs:** Two audiences, their actual conventions and a candidate principle.

**Operation:** Find a familiar entry cue and an unfamiliar consequential relation. Preserve the relation while adapting presentation or learning sequence. Record which users can understand and create with it.

**Construction:** Teach an action-game player a routing mechanic through a familiar dodge/knockback encounter before asking for an authored autoplay policy. A music study would separately inspect actual listening conventions rather than infer them from genre labels.

**Comparison:** Existing presentation, a conventional tutorial and a version with the unfamiliar relation removed.

**Outcome:** Comprehension, unaided construction and audience-specific uptake; familiarity and skill are measured separately.

**Defeating observation:** The bridge only increases clicks, replaces the distinctive relation or benefits solely from more instruction time.

**Basis:** FS03, FS04, FS09 as attributed crossover accounts. **Claim target:** access, not component invention.

methods.title: FO04 — Generate a family before polishing a flagship
methods.source_block:
## FO04 — Generate a family before polishing a flagship

**Inputs:** A seed rule and a small set of declared variation axes.

**Operation:** Produce a normal instance, a boundary case, an inversion and a counterexample. For each, state the shared relation, changed decision and known equivalent. Repair the grammar if it needs a special exception for every member.

**Construction:** Apply movement-to-consequence control to destination, time, capacity and authorization. Keep effects and stage resources explicit.

**Comparison:** Ordinary brainstorming under the same source information, candidate count and construction budget.

**Outcome:** A family with multiple valid consequential variants and disclosed equivalence, rather than raw output volume.

**Defeating observation:** Variants are decorative, invalid or interchangeable; the ordinary route generates the same useful family with less effort.

**Basis:** FS10, FS12, FS13. **Claim target:** generative yield under bounded conditions.

methods.title: FO05 — Lower the cost of making, without fixing the answer
methods.source_block:
## FO05 — Lower the cost of making, without fixing the answer

**Inputs:** A difficult practice, its required knowledge and the intended new creators.

**Operation:** Identify one entry barrier. Supply a representation, constrained editor or teaching aid that preserves substantive choices. Then ask users to create without the aid or with a new instance after a delay.

**Construction:** An autoplay editor exposes observable state and six ordered rules, with explanations of consequences. It leaves route, item and priority decisions to the player.

**Comparison:** A competent ordinary editor/tutorial with equivalent information; assisted output and delayed transfer are different outcomes.

**Outcome:** Entry time, viable constructions, variation and retained unaided performance.

**Defeating observation:** The tool supplies the strategy itself, only increases superficial variations or yields no retained ability beyond the baseline aid.

**Basis:** FS10, FS11 motivate examining representation and practice; they do not establish this intervention's efficacy. **Claim target:** access and learning.

selection_freeze.sequence: Written before searching for or reading the comparison novel and before selecting either passage window.
selection_freeze.anchor: Mary Shelley's Frankenstein, already encountered in supplied LS16; author cannot be blind to the anchor or its prestige.
corpus_criteria: Original English long prose fiction by Mary Shelley, to hold author and language constant.
A comparison first published from 1818 through 1833, with a dated primary title-page record or institutional bibliographic record.
Public-domain primary text freely accessible through a stable public URL.
Choose the earliest accessible novel after Frankenstein that meets the criteria; exclude autobiographical nonfiction and shorter tales.
The comparison is a curatorial less-canonized candidate only: no validated canonicity measure or causal endurance classification is available.
Retain unavailable candidates and edition uncertainty in the record; do not silently treat digital availability as historical survival.
selection_freeze.passage_rule: Take exactly the first 160 whitespace-delimited prose words of Chapter 1/I of each novel's main body, excluding title, chapter heading and preface. Preserve words and punctuation, normalize whitespace only, and record textual boundaries. This matches location and length, not a suspected feature. If edition differences cannot be resolved, report them rather than calling versions identical.
selection_freeze.coding_limits: Native structural/source audit only. No reader responses, canon score, representativeness, human effects or endurance causation may be inferred. Genre is broad novel/prose fiction; any narrower genre mismatch must be disclosed.
selection_freeze.author_blindness: Impossible: author knows the supplied classic anchor and will retrieve both title-bearing sources. Neutral A/B output can mask labels for later readers but cannot undo recognition or make this author blind.

data.execution_status: Input preparation only; no LL or FO strategy execution, participant study, listening analysis, game test or efficacy claim.

cases.title: The Dry Platform
cases.ending_disclosed: All twelve people survive dry and uninjured. Four seed cases are lost; the next planting uses two of six planned plots.
cases.narrative: Before the river rose, Mara pinned the gate diagram beside the gauge. Twelve people waited above the courtyard. Below them stood six seed cases. Opening the sluice would save the platform and wet the courtyard; moving the cases first required two helpers for eight minutes. Ivo pointed to the cart. Mara pointed to the four people still waiting for blankets. She would not borrow their helpers. At 06:05 she opened the gate. Water took the four low cases. Two on a high shelf stayed dry. By 06:12 all twelve people were wrapped and safe. At 06:20 the flood peaked below their boots. The next day, four germination checks failed. At the next planting Ivo marked out two plots, leaving four stakes without seed. Mara returned the diagram to its hook. Ivo left the empty cart beneath it.

event_ledger.fact: A public gauge predicts the flood peak at 06:20. Twelve evacuees wait on a raised platform; six seed cases lie in the lower courtyard.

The published gate diagram says opening the sluice keeps the platform dry but floods the courtyard. A two-helper cart move takes eight minutes. Moving helpers delays blankets for four evacuees by four minutes; no extra injury is guaranteed.
Ivo asks Mara to cart the six cases before opening the sluice. Mara declines because she will not withdraw the two helpers from warming duty.
Mara opens the sluice. Nobody carts the cases.
Water reaches four low seed cases. Two cases already on a high shelf stay dry.
All twelve evacuees are dry and have received blankets. Nobody is injured.
The flood peaks. The raised platform remains dry.
The four soaked cases are discarded after failed germination checks; the two dry cases remain viable. The next planting uses two of the six originally planned plots.

narrators.goal: Keep all twelve people safe without withdrawing warming helpers during the flood window.
narrators.text: I wanted all twelve people safe without withdrawing their warming helpers. I posted the 06:20 forecast and the diagram: opening the gate protected the platform and flooded the courtyard. I knew six seed cases were below it, and that two helpers could cart them in eight minutes, delaying four people's blankets by four minutes. At 06:04 Ivo asked me to move them first. I declined. At 06:05 I opened the sluice without a cart move. Four low cases soaked; two high cases stayed dry. By 06:12 everybody was dry, wrapped and uninjured; the 06:20 peak left the platform dry. Later four cases failed their germination checks. Two remained viable, so only two of six planned plots were planted. My decision met the immediate goal I chose. That does not make the lost seed disappear.

narrators.goal: Preserve six viable seed cases while accepting the declared temporary blanket delay.
narrators.text: I wanted all six seed cases viable as well as all twelve people safe. I accepted a four-minute blanket delay for four people if two helpers carted the cases during the eight minutes before the 06:20 flood peak. Mara had posted the forecast and the gate diagram: the platform would stay dry and the courtyard would flood. At 06:04 I asked for the cart move. She declined. At 06:05 she opened the sluice; nobody moved the cases. Four low cases soaked, and two high cases stayed dry. By 06:12 everyone was dry, wrapped and uninjured. At 06:20 the platform remained dry. Four cases later failed germination checks. The two viable cases supplied two of six planned plots. Her chosen immediate goal was met. My goal was not. I cannot claim from this record that my proposed delay would have caused no discomfort.

presentation.shared_packet: Give E01–E08, the same ending disclosure and the same chosen narrator account in every rhetoric condition.
presentation.literal: A mixed outcome: twelve people dry, four seed cases ruined, two of six plots planted.
presentation.ironic: A perfect victory: twelve people dry, four seed cases ruined, two of six plots planted.
presentation.controlled_dimension: Replace only the two-word evaluative phrase 'mixed outcome' with 'perfect victory'; both sentences contain the same 15 words by whitespace counting except that phrase, in the same order. Information is identical. No facts, timings, options or outcomes change.
presentation.tone_limit: The incompatible praise is an authored irony cue, not a validated stimulus. Recognition, liking and comprehension are unknown.
presentation.perspective_limit: Both accounts explicitly retain all ledger events. Different evaluations do not change the gate's available actions.
presentation.disclosure_limit: The bank discloses the ending. A future first-exposure condition needs a separately frozen neutral introduction; reading this bank destroys first-exposure ignorance.
presentation.counterfactual_limit: Ivo's plan is an unperformed alternative with a declared resource/time tradeoff; the record does not establish its injury outcome.

forbidden_inferences: No participant response or replay occurred.
The story is newly authored for this bank, not certified unprecedented.
Narrator testimony cannot add events absent from E01–E08.

cases.title: Arrival controls consequence
cases.exposure: Reuses the supplied Creature's Errand and four GF paper instances. This is exposure to existing seed material, not independent discovery; no output count is added.
game_envelope: Choose one hero from a roster of three.
Three stages, each with a boss; items appear during the run.
Manual control and player-authored autoplay are separate conditions.
Autoplay uses at most six ordered rules; first true predicate selects one legal action per tick.
frozen_local_rules: One courier carries exactly one charge. Its arrival at a dock consumes that charge and commits one public consequence exactly once. Courier death destroys the charge and is not arrival.

On each integer tick: apply the hero's legal action; apply damage/death; recompute the courier's shortest unblocked route; move the courier one cardinal cell; commit arrival; update public cooldowns. A killed courier cannot also arrive. No retroactive outcome changes.

Use a 9 by 5 unit grid, coordinates x=0..8, y=0..4. Courier starts (4,2), red dock (0,2), blue dock (8,2), hero (4,4). All cells are initially open. Distance is shortest cardinal path length. Choose the nearest reachable accepting dock; equal distance favors red. Among equal routes use left, up, right, down priority.

Red arrival spawns exactly two contact attackers; blue arrival supplies one defensive charge. These are declared consequences, not evidence of balanced value. Neither dock changes acceptance secretly.

Before tick 1 allow up to two walls, each costing one shared construction token. Walls cannot occupy a dock, courier or hero cell and cannot block both docks. Wall placement is irreversible during the stage.

Knockback moves the living courier two cells in a chosen cardinal direction, stopping before a blocked cell or grid edge; range is Manhattan distance at most three from the hero. It costs one finite charge, with a four-tick cooldown. Hero movement is one open cardinal cell per action.

The courier has two hit points; a hero strike within distance three removes one hit point and costs that tick's action. Reflect affects ordinary contact attackers and does not redirect the courier. Every hero must have a public legal route to strike or redirect; no courier immunity.
Public observation exposes positions, walls, route lengths/reachability, charge status, dock acceptance/state, hero resources and cooldown. Autoplay cannot use an unexposed shortest-path oracle.

Full boss/contact combat, hero-specific abilities, starting health/charges and item schedules are not supplied as an implementation. Freeze them equally across compared conditions before any survival/performance claim. The local rules define the courier micro-system only.
allowed_variants: Destination (GF01): red reinforcements versus blue defensive resource; ablate to identical dock consequences.

Time (GF02): one dock; disclose an accepting boss-phase window before play. Arrival within it grants one defensive charge; outside it spawns two attackers. Specify window and finite delay budget; no indefinite free stall.

Capacity (GF03): one-slot dock, two couriers, disclosed discharge schedule. Second arrival before discharge overloads into two attackers. Specify simultaneous-arrival order by courier ID; unlimited capacity is the ablation.

Authorization (GF04): an earlier public action supplies one expiring token. Arrival consumes it once to reduce a declared boss shield amount; no token adds that amount. Specify token lifetime and shield amounts before use. No hidden authority.
Vary one axis at a time for interpretation; presentation can vary without changing legal actions, observation, costs or rewards. Multiple axes require an explicit combined event order.

creator_payload.grammar: An entity carries a resource; arrival commits a consequence determined by public destination, time, capacity or authorization; legal movement changes that arrival.
creator_payload.obligations: Public state, finite costs, vulnerability, irreversible arrival, feasible response and six-rule interface. State a strong ordinary equivalent and the changed decision.

evaluator_only_holdout.withholding_rule: Fresh creators receive only the extracted creator_payload; they must not read this file, the source WORKED-FAMILY, parent history or evaluator holdout. This bank author and previously exposed agents are not blind and cannot claim withheld generalization. The withholding is a future information assignment, not a run already performed.

limits: No game implementation, balance test or performance trace was run.
Instruction under an assigned prompt is not cultural uptake.
A strong ordinary equivalent may explain the whole proposed relation.

cases.title: Future Classics documentary pack
cases.document_selection: Include all FS01–FS09 supplied documentary records, irrespective of apparent success. The source set existed before this bank and is a convenience sample. The following role coding is frozen for a later native audit; musical branch membership is not defined.

record_roles.catalog: Dated release identity or credits; copy/tags may be retrospective.
record_roles.testimony: Attributed creator recollection about intention, access or collaboration; not independent causal measurement.
record_roles.editorial: Observed claim language about a genre; not technical branch membership.
record_roles.missing: Unknown is retained as null, not zero or a negative finding.

documents.limit: Related earlier work; tag/copy creation dates and exact sonic relation to the narrower proposed branch are unknown.

documents.limit: Current promotional catalog; no audio listened to.

documents.limit: Direct HTML passages read. The 2020 remix project does not prove every collaborator descends from the 2015 album; artists also describe their own earlier influences.

observed_relations.relation: Credited source artist on Come In Peace (Vini Vici remix)
observed_relations.limit: A credit documents reworking/collaboration, not one-way generational descent; original track chronology not established here.
Peer, precursor, influence and descendant roles remain distinct and unresolved.

cases.classification_for_later_native_audit: Assign documentary role and date certainty only. Use bins before April 2015, April 2015, and after April 2015 through December 2020. Code sonic branch membership, earliest component invention, independent uptake, dropout, audience denominator and market share as unknown unless additional inspected evidence supports them. Do not create membership by resemblance inferred from biography.

framing.neutral: A 2015 psytrance album by Vini Vici on Iboga Records.
framing.title_context: The creators titled their 2015 psytrance album Future Classics.
framing.limit: Both are truthful descriptions; anticipated future status is a proposed interpretation of the title, not observed naming efficacy or verified acclaim.

cases.synthetic_policy: Synthetic descendant graphs may be authored later only as explicitly synthetic audit fixtures in separate records. They must never populate this pack's observed_relations or masquerade as actual musical lineage.

cases.title: Same-author opening-window comparison
cases.selection_result: Frankenstein (1818 edition) and Valperga (1823, volume I). Valperga is a curatorial less-canonized candidate, not a measured canon group. The earliest-accessible-novel criterion was searched through a targeted Gutenberg/UPenn discovery, not an exhaustive bibliography; earliest eligibility is not certified.
cases.matching: Same author, original English, five-year first-publication gap, main Chapter I opening, 160 words each. Gothic/scientific fiction versus historical fiction is a genre mismatch; narrator person and subject also differ. Neither historical reach nor present familiarity is controlled.

cases.native_audit_contract: A later investigator may code visible perspective, evaluations, causal connections, contrast and attributed claims in these actual windows, retaining exact evidence and disagreement. It may compare them to a classics-only inventory. It may not invent reader ratings, familiarity, return, appreciation change, curriculum frequency or a validated canon measure. The opening windows may contain none of the suspected feature; do not replace them to improve the finding.
cases.label_masking: A/B text can be passed without work titles to a fresh coder, but geographical/historical/name clues can identify it. This author has read the metadata and is not blind. Do not call A/B labeling a blinded reader study.
cases.availability_missingness: Both are digitally available now. Edition/translation histories, missing historical novels, publication runs, curriculum exposure and longitudinal readership were not gathered. A single accessible comparison does not put all forgotten works back into a corpus.

cases.title: Completion and return classification fixtures
cases.observation_window: Seven days; these are fictional input records, not measured players.

records.record: Completed three bosses on day 1; reports satisfaction; had access all seven days; no return by day 7; recalls the cost decision.
Stops at stage 1 on day 1 and reports frustration; access unavailable on days 2–7; no observed return.
Completes on day 1; returns voluntarily on day 2 with a changed routing plan and the same rewards; no further observation after day 3.
Still playing an unfinished run at the day-7 cutoff; no satisfaction or reason-for-stopping report.

cases.limits: Native agents can audit event definitions and censoring from these fixtures. They cannot estimate actual retention, causal discovery effects, population prevalence or participant satisfaction.

claim_ceiling: Actual native authoring and paper/documentary comparisons; no real human or game outcomes. Paired authored conditions within this one role, not randomized independent arms.
